hints.title: Bidirectional Tree Graph
hints.text: Convert the parent-child binary tree structure into an undirected adjacency graph, connecting each node to its left child, right child, and parent.

hints.title: Target Identification
hints.text: Locate the node whose value equals k, which serves as the starting vertex for path traversal.

hints.title: Shortest Path to Leaf
hints.text: Initiate a breadth-first search from the node with value k outward across the graph. The first node popped from the queue that was a leaf in the original tree is the closest leaf.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: Graph adjacency conversion followed by unweighted BFS to closest leaf.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Traversing only downward from k ignores closest leaves located in parent or sibling branches.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bidirectional graph modeling allows standard shortest path exploration in linear space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Model parent pointers so path distances upwards and downwards are explored symmetrically.
